newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel foreign minister to attend Malta conference.
newsitem.headline: Israel foreign minister to attend Malta conference.

text.p: Israel said on Monday Foreign Minister David Levy would attend Europe-Mediterranean talks in Malta but PLO officials said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat would not meet Levy at the conference.
"The foreign minster will leave tomorrow morning for Malta," said a Foreign Ministry spokesman. Earlier on Monday the spokesman said Levy was still considering whether to attend.
Palestinian officials said special European envoy to the Middle East Miguel Angel Moratinos has proposed that Arafat meet Levy to defuse a month-old crisis that has frozen Israeli-PLO peace talks.
But Arafat aide Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters before the PLO leader left Gaza on his way to Malta on Monday that no such meeting would take place.
"There won't be any meeting with Levy during the Malta conference," Abu Rdainah said.
Countries attending the two-day conference are due to discuss advancing the 27-member EU-Mediterranean Partnership created in Barcelona in 1995.

Israeli political commentators said Levy was concerned Arab states would exploit the forum to criticise Israel for its Jewish settlement policy but EU council president Hans van Mierlo said the Arabs have agreed not to raise the issue.
Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last month plunged peace moves with Palestinians into crisis and touched off a wave of Arab unrest in the West Bank and Gaza.
Palestinians view East Jerusalem as the capital of their future state and say the construction defies international law. Israel claims all of Jerusalem as its "eternal" capital.
